tool_args.rationale: The W1 bridge signature and archive note point to the node C two-layer siphon, but the current rows hold s_grad constant and give no branch-discriminating evidence. The cheapest relevant probe is open_branch_discriminating_probe (cost 2.0); acquire it before selecting and fitting a model.

considered_alternatives.option: Author the two-layer siphon model (node C / W1 bridge) now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The five observations vary only u_now; s_grad is fixed at 1 and H, x_now, and mem_conv are also fixed. The branch sign and sink response are therefore not identifiable.
No trajectory or memory-ODE evidence supports spending the higher cost on this probe; the listed W1 bridge maps to the simpler node C siphon.
It is explicitly irrelevant auxiliary data and would not resolve the branch/sink ambiguity.

considered_alternatives.option: Use a static Michaelis, quadratic, or other one-variable curve
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Such fits can mimic the observed u_now response but cannot distinguish the bridge siphon branch or identify its sink-gradient dependence.
